title: Break the Loop
subtitle: A treatment-strategy game about symptom feedback and the network theory of mental disorders.
learning_goals: Explain how reinforcing interactions between symptoms can sustain a high-activity network state.
Distinguish a one-time symptom intervention from changes to an interaction or a node's activation field.
Compare intervention strategies under a limited budget, including the cost of buying a probabilistic forecast.
creator: Denny Borsboom
notes: Prototype for review. Nine illustrative criteria-level nodes, not fitted patient data or a reproduction of Cramer et al.'s 14-node network. Random-scan Gibbs dynamics use a 0/1 Ising model. Paid forecasts enumerate 512 states exactly and show the all-inactive probability after six sweeps; they cost one coin and do not advance time. Node switches cost 1 coin and are one-time events; edge removal and 1.5-unit activation-field reductions cost 2 coins each and last for the round. The budget and score include every action price and a 1-coin fee for each undo. Reversing an action does not refund its price or earlier undo fees. Undo is unavailable at zero coins. Win only when all nine nodes are inactive together, checked after an intervention and each response sweep. A trophy and brief confetti burst celebrate the win. Creator, affiliation and default license are draft submission metadata to review before uploading.
